newsitem.title: CHINA: Asiasat sets November 1997 satellite launch.
newsitem.headline: Asiasat sets November 1997 satellite launch.

text.p: Hong Kong's Asiasat consortium is planning to launch its Asiasat 3 communications satellite in November 1997, the Xinhua news agency said.
Asia Satellite Telecommunications Holdings said in March it would use Russia's Proton rocket to put its third satellite into orbit next year.

It made the switch from Chinese Long March rockets, used to launch Asiasat 1 and 2, after a string of failures for China's commercial space programme. Possible delays in China's programme were the reason for the change, it said.
The Asiasat 3 orbiter would replace and improve on Asiasat 1, Xinhua quoted Chen Liqun, general manager of Asiasat's China business, as telling a Chinese satellite user's conference in Beijing.
Asiasat 3 is being built by Hughes Space and Communications International, a unit of General Motors Corp, with a $220 million loan from a 15-bank consortium.
